code: library(fastrel) set.seed(1) # for reproducibility ped <- sim_ped(1000) tail(ped, n = 3) # last 3 individuals ##           id   dadid   momid sex ## 998  ind0998 ind0959 ind0989   1 ## 999  ind0999    <NA> ind0912   1 ## 1000 ind1000 ind0879 ind0871   1 A <- fastrel_ped(ped) # same as fastrel_vec(ped$id, dadid = ped$dadid, momid = ped$momid) A[998:1000, 998:1000] # relatedness matrix between those 3 individuals ##            ind0998    ind0999    ind1000 ## ind0998 1.03676886 0.06467905 0.10907260 ## ind0999 0.06467905 1.00000000 0.03918678 ## ind1000 0.10907260 0.03918678 1.05214919 max(diag(A) - 1)   # maximum inbreeding coefficients ## [1] 0.3335501

text: sim_pop() simulates population births, deaths, emigration immigration, returns step individual arrives leaves. replay store, adding arrivals removing departures step, record mean relatedness among individuals present:  Although 27150 individuals simulated total, store never held hundred :
code: rel <- rel_new() set.seed(1) pop <- sim_pop(n_steps = 1000, n_init = 200) # simulate pop (fine tuning the life history is possible) head(pop) # first 6 simulated individual life histories (no dadid and momid since founder) ##            id dadid momid sex arrival exit      fate  origin ## 1 ind00000001  <NA>  <NA>   1       0   20 emigrated founder ## 2 ind00000002  <NA>  <NA>   2       0    7      dead founder ## 3 ind00000003  <NA>  <NA>   1       0    2      dead founder ## 4 ind00000004  <NA>  <NA>   1       0    7      dead founder ## 5 ind00000005  <NA>  <NA>   2       0    3      dead founder ## 6 ind00000006  <NA>  <NA>   1       0   22      dead founder mean_relatedness <- data.frame(step = 0:1000, mean_rel = NA) # record mean relatedness for (t in 0:1000) {   rel_add(rel, pop[pop$arrival == t, c("id", "dadid", "momid")])   rel_remove(rel, pop$id[!is.na(pop$exit) & pop$exit == t])   A <- rel_get(rel)   mean_relatedness[mean_relatedness$step == t, "mean_rel"] <- mean(A[upper.tri(A)]) } plot(mean_rel ~ step, data = mean_relatedness,      type = "l", las = 1,      ylab = "Mean relatedness", xlab = "Time step") rel_size(rel)     # individuals currently in the store ## [1] 241

title: fastrel: fast relatedness, relationship and kinship matrices from pedigrees — fastrel-package
text: Two interfaces compute relatedness matrix : fastrel_ped() fastrel_vec() compute whole matrix pedigree one go, given data frame vectors (latter fast replacement 2 * kinship2::kinship()). rel_new(), rel_add(), rel_remove() rel_get() maintain matrix incrementally, computationally much cheaper pedigree keeps growing, individual-based simulation. rel_ids(), rel_size() rel_capacity() describe content store, rel_save() rel_load() save disk restore . rel_copy() makes independent copy . fastrel_inv() computes inverse relatedness matrix (precision matrix used animal models) sparse matrix, directly pedigree, can obtained even large pedigrees. sim_ped() simulates pedigree, sim_pop() population births, deaths, emigration immigration, testing benchmarking. README package, https://github.com/courtiol/fastrel website package, https://courtiol.github.io/fastrel/, gives overview worked examples: relatedness whole pedigree, incremental updates simulation births deaths, metapopulations, benchmarks packages.

code: rel <- rel_new()  ## founders: unknown parents rel_add(rel, data.frame(id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"), dad = NA, mom = NA))  ## births: the columns are found by their names, in any order rel_add(rel, data.frame(sire = c("B", "D"), dam = c("A", "C"), animal = c("E", "F"))) rel_add(rel, data.frame(id = "G", dad = "F", mom = "E"))  ## deaths (or emigration): free the slots rel_remove(rel, c("A", "B", "C", "D")) rel_size(rel) #> [1] 3 rel_ids(rel) #> [1] "E" "F" "G"  ## a mother-son mating rel_add(rel, data.frame(id = "H", dad = "G", mom = "E"))  A <- rel_get(rel) A #>      E    F    G    H #> E 1.00 0.00 0.50 0.75 #> F 0.00 1.00 0.50 0.25 #> G 0.50 0.50 1.00 0.75 #> H 0.75 0.25 0.75 1.25 diag(A) - 1   # inbreeding coefficients #>    E    F    G    H  #> 0.00 0.00 0.00 0.25  rel_get(rel, metric = "kinship")   # other measures: see ?relatedness_metrics #>       E     F     G     H #> E 0.500 0.000 0.250 0.375 #> F 0.000 0.500 0.250 0.125 #> G 0.250 0.250 0.500 0.375 #> H 0.375 0.125 0.375 0.625  ## an independent copy, e.g. to explore two scenarios from the same state rel2 <- rel_copy(rel) rel_remove(rel2, "H") rel_ids(rel)    # unchanged #> [1] "E" "F" "G" "H" rel_ids(rel2) #> [1] "E" "F" "G"  ## two patches: one store, and the patch of each individual kept aside rel <- rel_new(remember_removed = "id") rel_add(rel, data.frame(id = c("a1", "a2", "b1", "b2"), dad = NA, mom = NA)) patch <- c(a1 = "A", a2 = "A", b1 = "B", b2 = "B") rel_add(rel, data.frame(id = "a3", dad = "a2", mom = "a1"))   # born in A patch["a3"] <- "A" patch["a3"] <- "B"                                            # a3 moves to B rel_add(rel, data.frame(id = "b3", dad = "a3", mom = "b1"))   # and breeds there patch["b3"] <- "B" rel_get(rel, names(patch)[patch == "B"]) #>     b1 b2  a3  b3 #> b1 1.0  0 0.0 0.5 #> b2 0.0  1 0.0 0.0 #> a3 0.0  0 1.0 0.5 #> b3 0.5  0 0.5 1.0 rel_get(rel)["b3", "a1"]   # b3 is related to its grandparent in patch A #> [1] 0.25  ## with remember_removed = "id", a removed individual cannot come back rel_remove(rel, "a3") try(rel_add(rel, data.frame(id = "a3", dad = NA, mom = NA))) #> Error : some focal IDs were removed from the store earlier and cannot be added again: a3
